title: The Human Digestive System
text: The human digestive system breaks down food into nutrients that can be absorbed into the bloodstream. Digestion begins in the mouth, where salivary amylase starts breaking down starches. Food travels down the esophagus to the stomach, where hydrochloric acid and pepsin digest proteins. The partially digested food (chyme) moves into the small intestine, where enzymes from the pancreas and bile from the liver complete digestion. Nutrients are absorbed through the villi of the small intestine into the blood. Water is absorbed in the large intestine, and waste is expelled. The digestive process takes approximately 24–72 hours from ingestion to elimination.
